method: Independent agent with no conversation fork; only the saved blind brief containing tables/prompts/options, no answer fields or hints. No personal records.
input: Original blind brief had an imprecise blanket same-respondent description; corrected production data note after review.

answers.scale: The bus share rose by 10 percentage points, a 25% increase relative to 2016.
answers.from-to: The bus share rose from 40% to 50% between 2016 and 2024.
answers.compareFirstDraft: In Lakeford in 2024, trams accounted for 60% of the main commuting modes, compared with 30% for buses.
answers.compareRecommended: In Lakeford in 2024, 60% of respondents mainly commuted by tram, compared with 30% by bus.
answers.independent: Overall, the share commuting mainly by car declined, while the shares for bicycles and other modes increased. The car share fell from 60% in 2018 to 40% in 2024, a decrease of 20 percentage points. Over the same period, the bicycle share rose from 20% to 30%, an increase of 10 percentage points.

reviewerFindings: scale has one correct option; from-to has one repair under its explicit one-preposition constraint.
compare is intentionally open: levels, ratio/half, percentage-point difference and correctly based relative difference can all be valid.

The first compare draft describes a share of modes imprecisely; the recommended respondent-share version is clearer and is included in finite references. Do not treat the first draft as a proven model answer.
Clarify each city's and year's denominator; samples need not be the same individuals and no sample counts are provided.
Other is an aggregate; its overall increase does not prove every mode inside it increased.
Largest category does not mean majority: the car share is 40% in 2024.
Tram vocabulary may burden beginners; add the Chinese gloss.
This is bounded near transfer with data selection and an independently chosen overview, not a full IELTS assessment or evidence of distant mastery.
finiteNearBoundaries: 40% to 50%: by 10% is not by 10 percentage points; relative increase is 25%.
60% versus 30%: 30% higher would be 39%; 100% higher is 60%; 200% higher would be 90%.
A single-year cross-section cannot support a temporal doubling claim.
Percentages alone cannot establish absolute commuter counts, causes, individual switches or future trends.
productionCorrections: Added per-city/per-year denominator and sample-size note
Added aggregate Other and largest/majority self-check
Kept six independently proposed natural comparison references
scoringBoundary: Finite reference matches have no mastery, delayed evidence, transfer badge or IELTS score side effect; unmatched expression and open paragraph remain pending human review.
